Maintenance Report — MNT-0081-002

Asset: WELL-0081 (SW-24 Well 081, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 27 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 28 Jan 2023 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 19 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0081-0012 on 2023-01-26 Report written: 29 Jan 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0081-0012 at 09:45 on 2023-01-26 found crude oil on the pad: about 6.7% of the pad area, estimated 1.7 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 392 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 314 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0081-002 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.51% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0081-008

Asset: WELL-0081 (SW-24 Well 081, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 08 Oct 2023 08:00 · Finished: 24 Oct 2023 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 396 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0081-0047 on 2023-10-05 Report written: 24 Oct 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0081-0047 showed the wellhead at 33.0 °C with the air at 25.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 14 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 6 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0081-013

Asset: WELL-0081 (SW-24 Well 081, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: wellhead Work started: 05 Apr 2024 08:00 · Finished: 09 Apr 2024 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 110 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0081-0072 on 2024-04-04 Report written: 10 Apr 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the inspector saw a thin film of oil on the wellhead. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0081-0072 showed the wellhead at 29.4 °C with the air at 20.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The packing rings were worn and the polished rod was lightly scored. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because the replacement part was back-ordered from the supplier.

Root cause

Packing wear sped up by a slightly misaligned polished rod.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Closed the wellhead valves and bled off pressure.
  2. Removed the old packing.
  3. Installed new packing rings and adjusted the gland.
  4. Cleaned the wellhead area.

Summary of the fix: replaced stuffing box packing.

Testing and return to service

Checked the stuffing box with the unit running: no leak. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Fished and replaced parted rod section
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0081-022

Asset: WELL-0081 (SW-24 Well 081, T350, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 24 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 26 Aug 2025 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 49 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0081-0144 on 2025-08-21 Report written: 28 Aug 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running but the wellhead was cold and the rod load had dropped. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0081-0144 showed the wellhead at 38.2 °C with the air at 35.8 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod.

Root cause

Fatigue failure of a rod body, probably started by corrosion pitting.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Sucker rods4,495
Rod couplings1,124
Fishing tool rental1,873
Labour (company crew)6,643
Total14,135

Compliance check

WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-07MetWritten 2 days after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Consider corrosion inhibitor treatment for this well.
  • Keep the recovered rod for failure analysis.
